title.value: Measuring the Knowledge Acquisition-Utilization Gap in Pre-trained Language Models
title.justification: The paper focuses on evaluating the gap between knowledge acquisition and actual utilization in pre-trained language models, without specific emphasis on sustainability.
title.quote: Measuring the Knowledge Acquisition-Utilization Gap in Pre-trained Language Models Amirhossein Kazemnejad1,2 Mehdi Rezagholizadeh3 Prasanna Parthasarathi3† Sarath Chandar2,4,5†

extractions.description: This paper proposes a systematic framework titled XT RA E VAL to measure the parametric knowledge utilization in pre-trained language models (PLMs). It explores the gap between what models acquire in terms of knowledge and what they can actually utilize in downstream tasks. The study finds significant gaps in models' robustness and generalization capabilities, especially under distributional shifts. The framework evaluates how the size and scaling of models affect these knowledge gaps.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper mainly addresses technical aspects of knowledge utilization in language models and does not focus on climate or ecological sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: While pre-trained language models (PLMs) have shown evidence of acquiring vast amounts of knowledge, it remains unclear how much of this parametric knowledge is actually usable in performing downstream tasks. We propose a systematic framework to measure parametric knowledge utilization in PLMs.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not address climate or ecological sustainable development themes directly.
primary_category.quote: Our framework first extracts knowledge from a PLM’s parameters and subsequently constructs a downstream task around this extracted knowledge.
